freezone_to_mainland.name: Free Zone Mainland Operating Permit
freezone_to_mainland.legislation: Dubai Executive Council Resolution No. 11 of 2025
freezone_to_mainland.status: Fully operational in 2026. Free zone companies can obtain DET permits or licences to operate onshore in mainland Dubai.
freezone_to_mainland.apply_via: Invest in Dubai platform (digital application; requires a Dubai Unified Licence)

permit_types.period: 6 months, renewable at the same fee

freezone_to_mainland.phase_one_scope: Non-regulated activities only (tech, consultancy, design, professional services, trading). Regulated sectors (finance, healthcare, education, real estate) are deferred to a later phase.
freezone_to_mainland.regularisation_status: Article 13 required existing free zone establishments conducting activity in mainland Dubai to regularise within one year from the Resolution's effective date. Article 15 made the Resolution effective on publication in Official Gazette issue 707, published 21 March 2025, producing a 21 March 2026 deadline. The Director General may grant one extension for the same period where necessary; this pack does not assert that an extension is automatic or that a particular establishment received one. Confirm current status with DET before relying on the deadline.
freezone_to_mainland.tax_note: Keep separate financial records for mainland activities. Corporate-tax treatment depends on QFZP status, income classification and any domestic permanent establishment; the permit does not make all mainland-sourced revenue automatically taxable at 9%.

developments_2026.headline: District IO innovation district launched at DSO/DIEZ (AED 12.8bn expansion)
developments_2026.summary: AED 12.8 billion of expansion projects for Dubai Silicon Oasis under DIEZ. District IO (AED 11bn, 25 energy-efficient buildings including 18 commercial, phase one from 2026, phase two 2027) targets smart mobility, 3D printing, robotics, AI, quantum, Web3 and X-Tech, with incentives including end-to-end setup, funding support, flexible leasing and RegLab product testing without operational licences. Block 14 (AED 1.8bn, transit-oriented development near the Metro Blue Line) completes 2029.

developments_2026.headline: Meydan launches fully remote non-residency setup with a guaranteed corporate account via MPlus
developments_2026.summary: Fully remote company formation: founders anywhere can obtain a UAE trade licence online in as little as 60 minutes (24 hours for complex structures) across 2,500+ activities, then open a corporate bank account via Meydan's MPlus banking team (26+ banking partners, up to 17 currencies) without travelling to the UAE. Marketed as a guaranteed bank account with the licence.
developments_2026.caveat: Single-source Gulf News company-news item. Treat the guaranteed-account claim as marketing until verified directly with Meydan.

developments_2026.headline: Dubai South announces 2026 incentive package
developments_2026.summary: New incentives covering support for new company formation, facilitation of licence renewals, and exemptions from late-renewal fines. Detailed financial terms were not publicly disclosed; benefits are applied case by case on application to the free zone authority.

developments_2026.headline: DMCC crosses 26,000 members and signs a Tether MoU
developments_2026.summary: DMCC signed an MoU with Tether covering blockchain and payment infrastructure within DMCC, tokenisation advisory and ecosystem programmes. DMCC reports 26,000+ member companies including 4,000+ tech firms; the Crypto Centre crossed 700 members (38% YoY growth). DMCC also announced a Crypto.com commodities-tokenisation partnership and launched DMCC Quantum in H1 2026.

developments_2026.headline: Al Selmiyyah Defence Industrial Free Zone announced in Abu Dhabi (outside Dubai)
developments_2026.summary: Tawazun Council and AD Ports Group announced a defence industrial free zone in Abu Dhabi aimed at global defence OEMs, domestic production, technology transfer and SME participation in defence supply chains, under the Operation 300bn industrial strategy. No size, timeline or investment figures disclosed yet. Outside Dubai; noted for completeness only and not part of the Dubai zone matrix.

free_zones.full_name: Dubai International Financial Centre, Innovation Licence

visas.tiers_described: Up to 4 visas on a flexi-desk. More requires a private office in DIFC.

banking.notes: Bank acceptance depends on the bank and applicant. No official acceptance rating is published for this zone.

restrictions: No regulated financial services (DFSA licence required separately)
No virtual asset or crypto exchanges
